story.text: Where did a €180,000 washing plant spend €202,000?
Read every order line on the project.
Line one is "Hydraulic power unit, lift set B (2024)" from Levantis, €31,500: lift equipment on a washing plant.
Two accruals, €11,032 and €3,444, sit on the same order in the ledger.
Without that line the forecast is €170,817: inside the budget and inside the 10% rule.
Ask the project manager whether the unit belongs here before any change request is raised; if not, move it to the lift programme and withdraw the breach.

story.text: If nothing can be saved, say so: is there a fix inside the project?

lifecycle.flow: 4 November 2026: every human input is taken once, at the start. A one-off goal plans, asks only what it could not find, agrees the deliverables and the template for each, then runs to the end by itself: findings accepted automatically, the top option chosen automatically, the deliverables built. A standing goal agrees the same at set-up plus the actions it may take; when it fires it runs, chooses, acts, builds and tells you. Anything can be changed afterwards; the deliverables are rebuilt as the next version.

panelTabs.rule: Always the same six tabs in the same order, from the first message to the last. A tab with nothing in it yet says what will land there. The panel opens on the tab that matters at that moment (Plan while briefing, Workflow while it runs, Deliverables when it is done); the order never changes.

contents.plan: Open points (Missing in orange until answered, then Clarified in green with the answer and where it came from), then the plan rows and the deliverables agreed
contents.workflow: The steps as a graph; a "working now" card per running step with its calls one by one, a progress bar and the seconds elapsed
contents.findings: Every finding (tagged "Accepted automatically"), its evidence and data, and all the options with "Why this" and "Use this instead". On a standing goal also the runs and the actions with their states
contents.deliverables: The deliverables, built part by part in front of you (a chip per deliverable: done, being built, waiting), then complete; download or open in Submissions

stages.reading: The agent reads what it was given and what is connected (about twenty seconds at normal pace). The feed in the chat shows one tool call per line; each line reveals plan rows. The composer is off. Ends with the steps drafted.
stages.questions: Your input, all of it in one step. Only what the reads could not find, one card at a time (kind 'q'); each answered point turns from Missing to Clarified on the Plan tab. Then the deliverables card (kind 'deliv'): the deliverables the goal suggests, ticked, and more offered unticked; add your own in words; for each the template, Recommended, From the library, Upload your own or Create one for me. A standing goal's card also sets each kind of action to By itself or Ask me first. One click: Run it, or Arm the watch.
stages.running: (once) No second agreement and no checkpoint. Steps run (about ten seconds each); findings land as steps finish; then findings accepted automatically (over['acc:<id>'] = 'auto'), the top option chosen automatically (chosenBy 'auto'), the deliverables built part by part (prog: {sids, i, shown}). Status 'delivered'; the goal moves to Executed.
stages.armed: (watch) Armed. Nothing runs until the rule fires or the schedule is due ("Simulate the 22 September snapshot" or 'Simulate: run now' in the demo). On firing: a notification; status 'fired' while the steps run; then accept, choose, build and act by themselves: actions set to By itself are done, the others wait (state 'waiting') under Needs you until Approve or Leave it. Status 'executed'; a notification says what it found, what it chose and what it did. The watch stays armed.
stages.after: Look back, change anything: 'Use this instead' on another option, or a steer in the chat ("Carry the four at posted plus open orders": step 2 and everything after it re-run). Every deliverable is rebuilt as the next version (version, basis; the earlier version stays in the log). On a standing goal, what was done stays done and the new option's actions wait for your OK.

Ask the project manager whether the unit belongs here before any change request is raised; if not, move it to the lift programme and withdraw the breach.

The lift project at the same depot is €10,000 under its €400,000 budget.

story.text: The rule fired: P-VM-046 is more than 10% off its budget. What can still be done?

Read the seven order lines: €161,960 ordered, €145,960 received, €16,000 to come.
Posted plus open lines gives €194,000: still over, but 7.8% rather than 12.4%.
The controller asked for exactly this re-forecast by Wednesday.
Nothing in the register carries the overrun; a change request is the only instrument that moves the approved figure.
Publish a September snapshot at €194,000 and raise a €14,000 change request with it, so the review on Monday approves a known overrun instead of finding one.

story.text: Where did a €180,000 washing plant spend €202,000?

Line one is "Hydraulic power unit, lift set B (2024)" from Levantis, €31,500: lift equipment on a washing plant.
Two accruals, €11,032 and €3,444, sit on the same order in the ledger.

story.text: If nothing can be saved, say so: is there a fix inside the project?

Cancelling what is left saves at most €3,000 against a €22,317 gap, and would leave the plant without its as-built file.
The lift project at the same depot is €10,000 under its €400,000 budget.

recs.title: Re-forecast from the ledger today and raise a change request for the remainder
recs.summary: Replace the June snapshot with a September one built from the posted €178,000 and the €16,000 still to receive: €194,000, 7.8% over. Raise a change request for €14,000 so the overrun is approved rather than discovered.
recs.tradeoff: Puts the overrun on paper, which the project has avoided for nine months; the 7.8% depends on the open lines being all that is left, and the lift-unit question (recommendation 2) can still change the figure.

story.text: The rule fired: P-VM-046 is more than 10% off its budget. What can still be done?
Read the June snapshot: €202,317 forecast, 12.4% over.
The snapshot is three months old; since then €34,683 has posted and the ledger stands at €178,000.
Read the seven order lines: €161,960 ordered, €145,960 received, €16,000 to come.
Posted plus open lines gives €194,000: still over, but 7.8% rather than 12.4%.
The controller asked for exactly this re-forecast by Wednesday.
Nothing in the register carries the overrun; a change request is the only instrument that moves the approved figure.
Publish a September snapshot at €194,000 and raise a €14,000 change request with it, so the review on Monday approves a known overrun instead of finding one.

recs.title: Check the €31,500 lift power unit booked to the plant; if it belongs to the lift programme, move it and the breach disappears
recs.summary: PO-4500012207/10 is a hydraulic power unit for lift set B. Charged to the right project, the washing plant lands at €170,817, 5.1% under budget, and the lift programme absorbs a cost that is its own.
recs.tradeoff: If the unit is genuinely part of the washing plant installation there is no saving, and the question costs a week; if it is miscoded, the overrun was never real and the lift programme has to take the cost.

story.text: Where did a €180,000 washing plant spend €202,000?
Read every order line on the project.
Line one is "Hydraulic power unit, lift set B (2024)" from Levantis, €31,500: lift equipment on a washing plant.
Two accruals, €11,032 and €3,444, sit on the same order in the ledger.
Without that line the forecast is €170,817: inside the budget and inside the 10% rule.
Ask the project manager whether the unit belongs here before any change request is raised; if not, move it to the lift programme and withdraw the breach.

recs.title: No saving left inside the project: accept the overrun and re-baseline to €202,000
recs.summary: The plant is 98.9% spent and in commissioning. €3,000 is uncommitted and €16,000 is still to receive, most of it already delivered, so no cut inside the project closes a €22,000 gap. Re-baseline, and cover it from the Les Aubiers lift underrun (P-VM-021, €10,000 under) and portfolio contingency.
recs.tradeoff: Honest and quick, but it re-baselines a project that never raised a change request, and it spends another project’s underrun before that project has finished.

story.text: If nothing can be saved, say so: is there a fix inside the project?
Read the June snapshot: €3,000 uncommitted, €0 contingency.
Read the open order balances: €16,000 across six lines, €2,000 to €3,000 each, the work largely delivered.
Cancelling what is left saves at most €3,000 against a €22,317 gap, and would leave the plant without its as-built file.
The lift project at the same depot is €10,000 under its €400,000 budget.
There is no solution inside the project. Re-baseline to €202,000, take €10,000 from the lift underrun and €12,317 from portfolio contingency, and record why.
